summary: ADR-033 cites docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md, which does not exist (TKT-128 incidental)
description:
### Finding (incidental, surfaced during TKT-128 implementation)

`docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md:237` cites:

```
- `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` — recommendation R3, the originating finding
```

**That file does not exist.** Not on `main`, not on the `arch-review-in-place` branch, not anywhere
in history (`git log --all --diff-filter=A -- 'docs/reviews/*'` is empty; `docs/reviews/` is not a
directory in this repo). The 2026-07-25 architecture review was conducted in-session and its
recommendations were written straight into tickets (R3 → TKT-126/ADR-033, R4 → TKT-128), never into
a review file.

So an ADR's References section points a reader at provenance they cannot open. AGENTS.md says
documentation is 100% in-repo; a dead in-repo path is worse than no path, because it reads as if the
evidence exists somewhere.

### Why this is a separate ticket

Found while implementing TKT-128, which had the *same* dead link in its own ticket references.
TKT-128 avoided reproducing it (its ADR-004 amendment cites TKT-128/TKT-31 instead), but fixing
ADR-033 was outside its COS and would have been scope creep in a docs-only PR whose COS 5 pins the
diff to two files.

### Two ways to close it — decide, don't assume

1. **Re-point the citation** (smallest): ADR-033 cites TKT-126 for provenance, as ADR-004 now does
   for TKT-128. Reversible, no new artifact.
2. **Write the review file** the citations assume: reconstruct `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md`
   from the R1–Rn findings now living on the board. Bigger, and only worth it if the review has
   standing value beyond the tickets it spawned.

Recommendation: option 1 unless the owner wants the review preserved as a document.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No ADR references a path that does not exist in the repo.
- [ ] `grep -rn "docs/reviews" docs/` either returns nothing, or every hit resolves to a real file.
- [ ] Docs-only; no source changes.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### DoR — 8/8. Shaped 2026-07-28.

**Decision taken at shaping (owner call, delegated): option 1 — re-point the citation at
TKT-126.** The ticket's own recommendation, and ADR-004 already sets the precedent after
TKT-128. Option 2 (reconstructing `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md`) is only worth it if
the review has standing value beyond the tickets it spawned — it does not; R1–Rn all live on the
board with fuller context than the review had.

This mattered because the ticket is **`risk:low`**, which skips Gate 2 — an undecided approach
on a gate-skipping ticket gets decided unilaterally by the coding agent, with no human ever
seeing the choice. Decided here instead, so `risk:low` stays honest.

Verified at HEAD: `grep -rn "docs/reviews" docs/` returns exactly one hit, ADR-033:237.

**Verdict: READY.**

objective.note: ADR-033:237 cites docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md, which has never existed in this repo. AGENTS.md puts documentation 100% in-repo; a dead in-repo path reads as if evidence exists.

scope.note: IN: the ADR-033 References line, plus any other docs/reviews citation grep finds. OUT: reconstructing the 2026-07-25 review as a document (option 2, declined at shaping).

uncertainties.note: None left — the option-1/option-2 decision was the only one, taken at shaping.

dependencies.note: None. Docs-only; relates to TKT-126 (the work ADR-033 records) and TKT-128 (which hit the same dead link and avoided reproducing it).

approach.note: Option 1: re-point the citation at TKT-126, mirroring what ADR-004 now does for TKT-128. One line, reversible, no new artifact.

success.note: AC already crisp and grep-verifiable; grep -rn docs/reviews docs/ returns exactly the one hit today.

context_memo.note: ADR-033 is the artifact edited, not a constraint on the edit; no decision governs how an ADR cites provenance. Recorded as a reference rather than a governingAdr.
